examples.instruction: Generate a computer science project based on Python language.
examples.reference_output:
Title: Student Management System

Objective: The main aim of the project is to develop a Python-based student management system that can store, retrieve, and manipulate the data of students in schools and colleges.

Overview: The student management system is a program that allows users to enter, update, delete, and search for student data in an easy and efficient manner. This program will use a graphical user interface (GUI) to facilitate interaction with the user.

Tools and Technology: Python 3.X, SQLite Database, Tkinter GUI library.

Features:
- User-friendly GUI
- Add, update, delete and view student records
- Data is saved in SQLite Database
- Report generation in PDF format
- Search feature for efficient data retrieval

Methodology:

1. Design the main window using Tkinter GUI library which contains buttons like ADD, UPDATE, VIEW, DELETE, SEARCH and EXIT.

2. Create a database using SQLite and design a table named 'students' with columns like student ID, name, email, phone, address, and courses.

3. Define functions for each button, such as:
- ADD: This function will prompt the user to input details such as student ID, name, email, phone, address, and courses, and then add the details to the 'students' table in the database.
- UPDATE: This function will allow the user to update student information in the database.
- VIEW: This function will display the student data in a tabular form.
- DELETE: This function will enable the user to delete a particular student record from the database.
- SEARCH: This function will provide an efficient way to search for student data based on a particular field such as ID or name.
- EXIT: This function will terminate the program.

4. Develop a feature that generates reports in PDF format, including all student data or specific search results.

5. Test the program to ensure it is functional and debug any errors that may arise.

Conclusion:

By developing this Student Management System, institutions can improve their student data management and enhance their operations' efficiency. The program is user-friendly, and the graphical user interface makes it easy for users to interact with the system. The use of the SQLite database ensures that data is stored safely and can be retrieved easily. Overall, this project is an excellent tool for schools and colleges to manage their student data effectively.

examples.instruction: Write a script for a play about two friends.
examples.input:
Friends: Kate & Mia
Location: Mia's apartment
examples.reference_output:
(Setting: The living room of Mia's apartment. Kate is sitting on the couch, scrolling through her phone while Mia is in the kitchen, making coffee.)

Kate: (shouts) Hey Mia, do you have any plans for the weekend?

Mia: (shouts from the kitchen) Not really, just the usual errands and maybe some Netflix. Why do you ask?

Kate: (puts down her phone) I was thinking we could do something fun, maybe go to the beach or have a picnic in the park!

Mia: (enters, holding two mugs of coffee) That sounds like a great idea, Kate! I could use a break from my boring routine.

(Kate takes one of the mugs from Mia and takes a sip)

Kate: (smiling) Perfect! But if we're going to the beach, we'll need to go shopping for some cute swimsuits!

Mia: (sits next to Kate) Oh, I love shopping, count me in! But first, we need to make a list of all the things we'll need. Sunscreen, towels, snacks...

Kate: (interrupts) And a beach umbrella, I don’t want to get sunburnt!

Mia: (laughs) Good thinking, Kate, always looking out for me!

Kate: (smirks) That’s what friends are for! 

Mia: (leaning her head on Kate's shoulder) I don’t know what I would do without you.

Kate: (puts her arm around Mia) Same here, Mia. We’re going to have the best time at the beach!

(Both girls smile at each other, sipping their coffee, excited about their upcoming beach adventure.)

THE END

examples.reference_output:

Aged cheddar is a great option to include on a cheese platter because of its distinct, sharp flavor. This type of cheddar is aged for a longer period of time, typically 1-2 years, which results in a richer, more complex flavor. It has a crumbly texture that goes well with crackers, fruit or nuts.

Another popular choice is white cheddar, which is typically made from cow's milk or goat's milk, and has a creamy, smooth texture. This type of cheddar is milder in flavor, making it a great option for guests who prefer a less intense cheese.

Ultimately, the best type of cheddar cheese for a cheese platter is one that balances well with the other cheeses and accompaniments on the platter. Experiment with different options to find a combination that works for your taste preferences.

examples.instruction: Generate a list of tips to teach someone how to play chess.
examples.reference_output:
1. Start by learning the board: Chess is played on a square board divided into 64 squares of alternating colors. Each player starts with 16 pieces arranged on opposite sides of the board.

2. Know the pieces and their moves: Each piece has its own unique way of moving. The King can move in any direction, but only one square at a time. The Queen can move any number of squares along a rank, file, or diagonal. Rooks move horizontally or vertically, Bishops move diagonally, Knights move in an L-shape, and Pawns move forward but capture diagonally.

3. Understand the objective of the game: The ultimate goal of chess is to checkmate your opponent's King, which means it's in a position to be captured and there is no way to move it out of capture.

4. Learn the special moves: In addition to the regular moves, there are a few special moves. 'En passant' and 'castling' are two moves that can be useful in certain situations.

5. Develop a strategy: Chess is not just a game of moving pieces, but also a game of strategy. You'll want to control the center of the board, protect your King, and put pressure on your opponent's pieces.

6. Practice tactics: Chess tactics are moves that take advantage of the position of your opponent's pieces. Some common tactics include pins, forks, and discovered attacks.

7. Keep an eye on the clock: In a timed game, each player has a set amount of time to make all of their moves. This adds an extra element of strategy to the game, as players must balance the time they take to think with the need to make moves before time runs out.

8. Study endgame scenarios: The endgame is when there are only a few pieces left on the board. It's important to know how to maneuver your pieces to achieve checkmate, even with only a few pieces left.

9. Analyze your games: One of the best ways to improve at chess is to analyze your games after you've played them. Try to figure out what you did right, what you did wrong, and how you could have played better.

10. Play lots of games: Finally, the best way to learn chess is by playing it! Try to play as often as you can, against opponents of different skill levels. You'll improve quickly and have fun at the same time.

The ball should be similar in size and weight to a basketball.

The objective of the game is to score as many goals as possible while preventing the opposing team from scoring.

The game starts with a coin toss to determine which team will start with the ball. Each team must have an equal number of players. The team with the ball tries to score by throwing the ball over the net into the other team's half of the court. The opposing team must try to catch the ball and throw it back over the net to score.
